To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin resistance is more common in preterm newborn than term neonates.
insulin and HOMA IR levels were higher in preterm than in term newborn infants.

glucose, insulin, cortisol and HOMA levels in the cord blood are higher in term than in preterm newborn infants, and that insulin and cortisol are positively and negatively correlated with HMA, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early detection of insulin resistance in newborns, which may be useful for early detection of type 2 diabetic children.
the early alterations in the indices of glucose home-ostasis in term and pre-termed newborns.
the study of insulin resistance in preterm and term newborns and the relationship between insulin resistance and cortisol levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cord blood glucose levels are not different between the two groups, but the insulin levels were significantly higher in the preterm group.
preterm newborns have higher insulin levels and HIR values than term newborns and these values are correlated to the cortisol levels in both groups.
preterm newborns have higher insulin levels and Homa-IR values in cord blood, which support the theory of the intrauterine origin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin resistance in preterm infants is associated with higher cortisol levels and higher glucose levels.
the higher insulin resistance in the preterm newborns may be a consequence of intrauterine growth restriction and/or prematurity.
insulin and cortisol levels in cord blood of newborns are associated with insulin resistance and glucose homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the indices of glucose homeo-stasis are significantly different in preterm and term infants.

the early alterations in glucose homeostasis can be observed in the cord blood and the indices of glucose homeo- stasis in cord blood are useful in predicting the risk of metabolic diseases in later life.
the insulin resistance in newborns is a multifactorial phenomenon, and the role of cortisol in this phenomenon is still not clearly understood.
